title: Multi-agent verification of publication bundles for executable scientific submissions
abstract: A multi-agent verification system in which specialized agents independently inspect code, data, environment setup, workflow execution, and manuscript-artifact consistency will detect more reproducibility issues and generate more actionable feedback for executable scientific submissions than monolithic or checklist-based validation approaches. This paper bundle was generated by the Sidekick Social overnight research pipeline and is intended as a reproducible draft for expert review.
summary:
Research plan: A multi-agent verification system in which specialized agents independently inspect code, data, environment setup, workflow execution, and manuscript-artifact consistency will detect more reproducibility issues and generate more actionable feedback for executable scientific submissions than monolithic or checklist-based validation approaches.

Methodology:
- Define the core verification dimensions for executable scientific submissions, including artifact completeness, environment reproducibility, data accessibility, workflow executability, output regeneration, and claim-to-artifact consistency.
- Design a structured publication bundle format that exposes manuscript sections, code repositories, dependency manifests, datasets, execution instructions, expected outputs, and provenance metadata in machine-readable form.
- Assemble a benchmark corpus of executable scientific submissions and publication bundles across computational research domains, including a genomics-focused subset.
- Design a multi-agent architecture with specialized verifier agents such as repository integrity agent, environment agent, data access agent, execution agent, output comparison agent, and manuscript-consistency agent.
- Implement coordination logic that allows agents to share evidence, resolve conflicts, and produce a unified verification report with severity labels and remediation recommendations.
- Create gold-standard annotations from expert reviewers identifying reproducibility issues, failure severity, and minimum fixes needed for successful execution.
- Define evaluation metrics covering issue detection performance, execution success, report usefulness, verifier agreement, latency, and computational cost.
- Compare the multi-agent system with single-agent verification, static checklist review, and rules-based validation baselines.
- Run ablation studies to measure the value of specialization, inter-agent critique, and shared evidence aggregation.
- Develop deployment guidance for integrating publication-bundle verification into preprint screening, editorial triage, and reproducibility review workflows.

experiments: Benchmark multi-agent verification against single-agent and checklist-based approaches on labeled publication bundles using precision, recall, F1, and severity-weighted issue detection metrics.
Evaluate execution outcomes by measuring how often the system correctly predicts whether a bundle can be run to regenerate key outputs under a clean environment.
Run an ablation study removing specialized agents or inter-agent critique to determine which components most improve verification accuracy and report quality.
Test the system on genomics bundles to assess handling of large datasets, reference genome dependencies, workflow engines, and domain-specific software stacks.
Measure the actionability of generated verification reports by having expert reviewers and authors rate clarity, correctness, prioritization, and usefulness of remediation guidance.
Conduct robustness experiments on incomplete and adversarial bundles with broken paths, inconsistent metadata, missing dependencies, inaccessible data, and stale output artifacts.
Compare review efficiency by timing expert assessments performed with and without multi-agent reports and measuring changes in issue coverage and inter-reviewer agreement.
Analyze cost-performance tradeoffs across different agent coordination strategies, including parallel specialist agents, hierarchical review, and critique-refinement loops.
deliverables: A research paper describing the multi-agent verification framework, benchmark, and empirical results.
A benchmark dataset of executable scientific submissions, publication bundles, environment snapshots, and expert verification annotations where redistribution is allowed.
A reference publication bundle specification for executable submissions with validation-oriented metadata fields.
A prototype multi-agent verification system with reproducible evaluation scripts and documented interfaces.
A taxonomy of bundle verification failure modes and common reproducibility defects, including domain-specific findings for genomics.
A standardized evidence-linked verification report format for authors, reviewers, and editors.
Operational recommendations for incorporating multi-agent publication-bundle verification into scientific publishing workflows.
